butir.teks: Chapter Six: On the Afflictions of Knowledge, and an Explanation of the Signs of the Scholars of the Hereafter and the Evil Scholars

We have already mentioned what has been reported about the merits of knowledge and the scholars. Severe warnings have also been reported about the evil scholars, which indicate that they are the most severely punished of all creation on the day of the Resurrection.
So among the great essentials is knowing the signs that distinguish the scholars of this world from the scholars of the Hereafter. By the scholars of this world we mean

the evil scholars, whose aim in knowledge is to enjoy this world and to reach status and standing with its people. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "The people most severely punished on the day of the Resurrection will be a scholar whom Allah did not benefit through his knowledge." And from him (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said, "A person is not a scholar until he acts upon his knowledge." (١) The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Knowledge is of two kinds: knowledge on the tongue, which is Allah Most High's proof against His creation, and knowledge in the heart, which is the beneficial knowledge." (٢) He said, "At the end of time there will be ignorant worshippers and iniquitous scholars." (٣) He said, "Do not learn knowledge in order to boast with it over the scholars, to dispute with it with the foolish, or to turn people's faces toward yourselves with it. Whoever does that is in the Fire." (٤) He said, "Whoever conceals knowledge he has, Allah will bridle him with a bridle of fire." And he said, "There is something other than the Dajjal that I fear for you more than the Dajjal." It was said, "What is that?" He said, "The misleading leaders." (٥) He said, "Whoever increases in knowledge but does not increase in guidance increases only in distance from Allah." (٦) Jesus (peace be upon him) said, "How long will you describe the road to those who travel by night while you remain with the bewildered?" This and other reports indicate the gravity of the danger of knowledge, for the scholar is either exposed to eternal ruin or to eternal happiness, and by plunging into knowledge he has been denied safety if he does not attain happiness.
As for the reports (athar), 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "What I fear most for this community is the learned hypocrite."
They said, "How can he be a learned hypocrite?"
He said, "Learned of tongue, ignorant of heart and action."
al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Do not be among those who gather the knowledge of the scholars and the rare sayings of the wise, yet conduct themselves in action like the foolish."
A man said to Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), "I want to learn knowledge, but I fear that I will lose it." He said, "Abandoning knowledge is enough to lose it."

Ibrahim ibn 'Uyayna was asked, "Which of the people has the longest regret?" He said, "In the present world, the one who does good to someone who does not thank him; and at the time of death, the negligent scholar."

al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said, "Men are four: a man who knows and knows that he knows, so he is a scholar, so follow him; a man who knows and does not know that he knows, so he is asleep, so wake him; a man who does not know and knows that he does not know, so he is one seeking guidance, so guide him; and a man who does not know and does not know that he does not know, so he is ignorant, so shun him."
Sufyan ath-Thawri (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Knowledge calls out to action; if action answers it, well, and if not, it departs."
Ibn al-Mubarak said, "A person remains a scholar as long as he seeks knowledge, but when he thinks that he has come to know, he has become ignorant."

al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "I have mercy on three: the mighty man of a people who has become abased, the rich man of a people who has become poor, and a scholar with whom this world plays."
al-Hasan said, "The punishment of scholars is the death of the heart, and the death of the heart is seeking this world with the work of the Hereafter." And they recited:

I marvel at one who buys misguidance with guidance,
but one who buys his world with religion is more marvelous.

More marvelous than these two is one who sold his religion
for the world of another; he is more marvelous than both of them.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "A scholar will be punished with a punishment around which the people of the Fire will circle, deeming the severity of his punishment great." (١) By this he meant the wicked scholar.

Jesus (peace be upon him) said, "The likeness of evil scholars is that of a rock that has fallen at the mouth of a river: it does not drink the water, nor does it let the water reach the crops. And the likeness of evil scholars is the likeness of the drain of a latrine, its outside plastered with gypsum and its inside foul, and the likeness of graves, whose outside is well kept and whose inside is the bones of the dead." These reports and athar show that the scholar who is one of the children of this world is lower in condition and more severely punished than the ignorant man.

and that the successful ones brought near are the scholars of the Hereafter. They have signs. Among them is that he does not seek this world by his knowledge. For the lowest degree of the scholar is that he perceives the pettiness of this world, its baseness, its murkiness and its passing, and the greatness of the Hereafter and its permanence, the purity of its bliss and the majesty of its dominion; and that he knows that the two are opposites, that they are like two co-wives, whenever you please one you anger the other; that they are like the two pans of a scale, whenever one is heavier the other is lighter; that they are like east and west, whenever you come nearer to one you grow farther from the other; and that they are like two cups, one full and the other empty, so to the extent that you pour from it into the other until that one is filled, the first one empties.
For whoever does not know the pettiness of this world, its murkiness, the mixing of its pleasures with its pain, and then the passing away of whatever in it is pure, is unsound of mind.

For observation and experience guide to that. So how can he be among the scholars who has no intellect? And whoever does not know the greatness of the matter of the Hereafter and its permanence is an unbeliever stripped of faith, so how can he be among the scholars who has no faith? And whoever does not know the opposition of this world to the Hereafter, and that combining the two is hoping for what cannot be hoped for, is ignorant of the laws of all the prophets, indeed an unbeliever in the whole Qur'an from its beginning to its end, so how is he counted among the company of scholars? And whoever knows all this and then does not prefer the Hereafter over this world is a captive of Satan, whom his appetite has destroyed and whom his wretchedness has overcome, so how is he counted among the party of scholars whose degree is this? In the reports of David (peace be upon him), narrating from Allah Most High: "The least that I do to a scholar, when he prefers his appetite over My love, is to deprive him of the sweetness of intimate converse with Me. O David, do not ask about Me a scholar whom this world has intoxicated, for he will bar you from the path of My love. Those are the highway robbers upon My servants. O David, when you see a seeker of Me, be a servant to him. O David, whoever returns a fugitive to Me, I write him down as an assayer (jahbadh), and whoever I write down as an assayer, I never punish." For this reason al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "The punishment of scholars is the death of the heart, and the death of the heart is seeking this world with the work of the Hereafter."
For this reason Yahya ibn Mu'adh said, "The radiance of knowledge and wisdom goes away only when this world is sought with them."
Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "If you see the scholar frequenting the emirs"

he is a thief." 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "If you see a scholar who loves this world, suspect him regarding your religion, for every lover plunges into what he loves." Malik ibn Dinar (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "I read in some earlier books that Allah Most High says: The least that I do to a scholar, when he loves this world, is to remove the sweetness of intimate converse with Me from his heart."

A man wrote to a brother of his, "You have been given knowledge, so do not extinguish the light of your knowledge with the darkness of sins, for then you would remain in darkness on the day when the people of knowledge go forth in the light of their knowledge." Yahya ibn Mu'adh ar-Razi (may Allah have mercy on him) used to say to the scholars of this world, "O people of knowledge, your palaces are Caesarean, your houses Chosroan, your garments Zahiri, your sandals Goliathan, your mounts Qarunic, your vessels Pharaonic, your sins of the Jahiliyya, and your doctrines Satanic. So where is the Muhammadan law?" The poet said:

The shepherd guards the sheep from the wolf,
but how is it when the shepherds are wolves to them?
And another said:

O company of reciters, O salt of the land,
what can set the salt right if the salt itself spoils?

One of the knowers of Allah ('arif) was asked, "Do you think that one for whom acts of disobedience are the delight of his eye does not know Allah?" He said, "There is no doubt that one to whom this world is preferable to the Hereafter does not know Allah Most High."

And this is far below that. Do not think that leaving wealth is enough to join the scholars of the Hereafter, for status is more harmful than wealth. For this reason Bishr said, "'He narrated to us' is one of the doors of this world. When you hear a man say 'He narrated to us', he is only saying 'Make room for me.'"

Bishr ibn al-Harith buried some thirteen to nineteen book-cases and reed baskets of books, and he used to say, "I desire to narrate hadith, and if the desire to narrate had left me, I would narrate." He and others said, "When you desire to narrate, be silent, and when you do not desire it, narrate."

This is because taking pleasure in the status of imparting benefit and the position of guidance is a greater pleasure than every enjoyment in this world, so whoever answers his appetite in it is among the children of this world.

For this reason ath-Thawri said, "The trial of hadith is more severe than the trial of family, wealth, and children." How could its trial not be feared, when it was said to the master of the messengers (peace and blessings be upon him), ⟦QS 17:74⟧ Sahl (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Knowledge, all of it, is this world, and the part of it that belongs to the Hereafter is acting upon it; and all action is scattered dust except sincerity."

He said, "The people are all dead except the scholars; the scholars are all intoxicated except those who act; those who act are all deluded except the sincere; and the sincere one remains fearful until he knows with what it will be sealed for him."

Abu Sulayman ad-Darani (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "When a man seeks hadith, or marries, or travels in search of a livelihood, he has inclined toward this world." By this he meant seeking high chains of transmission (isnad), or seeking hadith that is not needed in seeking the Hereafter. Jesus (peace be upon him) said, "How can he be one of the people of knowledge whose journey is to his Hereafter while he is facing the road of his world? And how can he be one of the people of knowledge who seeks speech in order to report it, not in order to act upon it?" Salih ibn Kaysan al-Basri said, "I met the elders, and they used to seek refuge in Allah from the wicked man who knows the Sunna."
